extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural applicants, peer reviewers, and NIH program/staff (research community involved in NIH grant review)
extracted.subtask_description: Announcement of temporary changes to NIH peer review processes (Jan–May 2026 Council cycle) describing how applications will be selected for discussion, what summary statements will contain, timing of score release, and expectations for reviewers and applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced percentage of applications discussed
rubrics_metrics.description: Committees will reduce the percentage of applications discussed in most meetings by voting to place applications into three groups (top, middle, lowest thirds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committees will vote for which applications to discuss in three groups: The top third (30 to 35 percent) will be discussed in the review meeting and considered for funding. The middle third will be designated as “competitive but not discussed” and considered for funding. The lowest third will be designated as “not competitive and not discussed.” This change is intended to allow nearly all review meetings to run within one day and make recruiting reviewers and rescheduling meetings easier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of middle third as 'competitive but not discussed'
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications in the middle third will be labeled 'competitive but not discussed' rather than being discussed during the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being designated 'competitive but not discussed' means an application is still eligible for funding consideration — Institutes and Centers will consider for funding all applications that are discussed plus all designated as competitive. This designation opens the possibility of funding when those applications align with high program priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplified summary statements — required components
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary statements will be simplified but must convey the application’s scientific merit to advisory Councils and IC program staff through a small set of required elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary statements will have: a sentence describing the degree of consensus in the committee vote; bullets describing the main score-driving points; written critiques from the three assigned reviewers; and, for discussed applications, the overall impact score. These elements are intended to provide necessary information while simplifying the statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release timing for scores and summary statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Scores will continue to be released quickly after meetings; summary statements will be released later in the Council round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH will release summary statements later in the Council round, while continuing to release scores within three business days of the meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding consideration policy under modified process
rubrics_metrics.description: Designation for discussion or as 'competitive' determines which applications Institutes and Centers will consider for funding under the temporary modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutes and Centers will consider for funding all applications that are discussed plus all designated as competitive (top and middle thirds). The agency states that an application’s likelihood of funding is not affected by these procedural designations because the middle third remains eligible when aligned with program priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of reviewers' full critiques and program staff advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Full written critiques by reviewers will continue to be available to applicants, and program staff will remain available to advise applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers' full critiques will continue to be available and program staff will remain available to provide advice to applicants despite the simplification of summary statements and reduced discussion rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to maintain high quality peer review while adjusting processes
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH intends that emergency modifications will not substantially degrade peer review quality while addressing review backlog.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Though some changes are needed to review the nearly 100,000 expected applications this fiscal year, those changes will not substantially degrade the peer review processes. NIH remains committed to accomplishing three full rounds of peer review this fiscal year, believing a canceled round would be harmful to applicants and the research enterprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation to help by serving as an NIH reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH asks researchers invited to serve on review panels to consider accepting to help address backlog and enable the modified process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How You Can Help: If you are invited to participate in an NIH review panel, please consider saying 'yes.' There are benefits to serving in NIH peer review, including flexibility in submitting applications, intellectual stimulation, interaction with colleagues, and an opportunity to give back. Resources and programs (Become a Reviewer, Information for Reviewers, NIH Early Career Reviewer Program) are provided to facilitate participation.
